stages.name: Balance of payments components
stages.title: Balance of payments components
stages.sub: What actually gets recorded in each part of the balance of payments.

steps.q: A UK car maker sells £5m of cars to France and buys £3m of French cheese. Which part of the current account records this £5m and £3m?
steps.right: The record of goods and services bought and sold abroad
steps.wrong: The record of interest and dividends paid abroad
steps.hint: Cars and cheese are goods being exported and imported, not money earned on investments.

steps.q: A UK pension fund owns shares in a German company and receives £2m in dividends this year. Is this payment for a good sold, or for owning an asset abroad?
steps.hint: No car or cheese changed hands here, only a return on money already invested.

steps.q: The UK government sends £1m of aid to a country hit by a flood, with nothing bought or sold in return. Does this belong with trade flows, or with income earned on investments?
steps.right: Neither, it is a one-way gift with no return
steps.wrong: With income earned on investments abroad
steps.hint: Aid is not payment for goods, and it is not a return on an asset either.

steps.q: A foreign government writes off £4m of debt owed by a poorer country, and a migrant brings £50,000 of savings with them when they permanently move country. Are these everyday trade or income flows, or one-off transfers of wealth and assets themselves?
steps.right: One-off transfers of wealth and assets themselves
steps.hint: Nothing is being bought or earned each year here, it is a single transfer of an asset or debt.

steps.q: A US company buys a UK factory outright, another US investor buys UK government bonds, and the Bank of England adds dollars to its reserves. Are these purchases of goods, or purchases of assets and holdings of foreign currency?
steps.right: Purchases of assets and currency holdings
steps.hint: A factory, bonds and reserves are all things owned, not things consumed.
